title: Detection of Critical Laboratory Values Using Real-Time Data Streaming in Clinical Routine
summary:
In hospitals, severely abnormal laboratory values may sometimes be overlooked or recognized too late. This can contribute to worsening health conditions and reduced patient safety. The aim of this study is to examine whether a technical alert system can reliably detect such critical laboratory values in real time from existing routine clinical data and automatically forward alerts.
For this purpose, laboratory values from adult patients treated on two cardiac surgical intensive care units at the Deutsches Herzzentrum der Charité will be analyzed over a period of three months. The data are obtained exclusively from routine care. The study does not influence patient treatment, because alerts will not be sent to the treating physicians. No additional examinations or procedures will be performed.
The study will assess whether the system detects critical values completely, correctly, and rapidly. During the final two weeks of the study, the performance of this technical system will also be compared with freely available language models. All data remain within the Charité infrastructure and will be anonymized after completion of the analysis.
conditions: Critical laboratory values in critically ill intensive care patients.

interventions.name:
The aim of the proposed research project is to investigate the feasibility of a real-time alert system for the automated identification of critical laboratory values and their timely, structured transmission to clinical recipients.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Age ≥ 18 years
Admission to one of the two intensive care units WD1i or WD2i of the Deutsches Herzzentrum der Charité
Analysis of laboratory values for the duration of the patient’s stay in one of the two specified intensive care units
Laboratory values collected between 18 March 2026 and 18 June 2026

None
